properties.statement:
`set_artifact_checksum`'s TWO DISPOSITIONS HAVE NO ANSWER FOR THE COMMONEST FIX THERE IS: THE CODE WAS WRONG AND NOW MATCHES INTENT THAT NEVER CHANGED. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, item 8.

HIS CASE: after aligning as-built to an ALREADY ACCEPTED Requirement, 'neither `design_holds` (no design meaning) nor `design_updated` (design moved; pass the ChangeEvent) fits cleanly if you ALSO revised a Decision in the same hour. Agents spend a turn picking a side instead of shipping the comparison fix.'

WHY NEITHER FITS. `design_holds` says the change carries no design meaning — but a bug that violated an accepted Requirement carried a great deal of it; the design was right and the code was wrong, which is a fact worth recording rather than waving through. `design_updated` says the design moved with the code — and it did not; the Requirement is untouched and passing a ChangeEvent for it would assert a revision that never happened.

⭐ THIS IS THE `change_type` GAP IN A SECOND VOCABULARY. `fact:defect-change-event-has-no-type-for-a-field-reported-defect` records that the enum has no value for 'the code was wrong'; here the DISPOSITION enum has no value for the same event. The same missing meaning is absent from two independent surfaces, which is evidence it is a real category rather than a wording quibble.

HIS PROPOSED VALUE, held open in `dec:idea-should-the-checksum-accept-have-an-as-built-aligned-disposition`: `as_built_aligned` — 'allow it when a Requirement did not change and the file now matches it'.

WHAT MUST NOT BE LOST IF IT IS ADDED: `dec:two-sided-accept` exists because a silent accept 'is how a design erodes into fiction over N fix cycles while reporting zero gaps'. A third disposition is only safe if it makes the SAME claim shape — dated, attributable, and counted apart in the confirmation ledger the way `baseline_established` already is.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how often this case arises. One report, and the confirmation ledger could answer it by counting `design_holds` accepts whose events carry `test_failure_fix` — a sweep nobody has run.
